themes.title: General-purpose humanoids
themes.description: Unitree's retail tranche was oversubscribed more than 8,000x — a record for STAR Market tech listings — and shares are set to begin trading this week (Aug 17-21, ticker 688836); 2025 revenue rose 335% YoY on 60% gross margins and the company is already profitable. BYD confirmed (Jul 28) it will unveil its first humanoid robot in August. Hyundai completed a $325M buyout of SoftBank's last Boston Dynamics stake (Jul 16), taking full ownership at an implied $3.3B valuation — modest next to headline humanoid marks. Tesla Optimus remains the outlier: the Fremont line was torn down in 46 days for the conversion, but formal production still hadn't started as of this week.

themes.title: Warehouse & logistics automation
themes.description: Still the most commercially proven sub-sector. Symbotic's Q3 FY26 revenue hit $721M (+22% YoY) with GAAP net income of $55M — the backlog is now converting to real, growing profit. Shares rose 3.9% on Aug 11 after Symbotic acquired UK software firm ARMS Innovations to extend into AI-driven warehouse-ops optimization, though sell-side consensus is a split Hold (PT $62.64).

themes.title: Surgical robotics
themes.description: ISRG's Q2 beat still hasn't stopped the bleeding — shares are down 32.6% YTD (~$395-402, market cap $139.4B) even with a $509 average price target. A Motley Fool fund manager reiterated a bullish call on Aug 12, but sell-side remains split. J&J Ottava and Medtronic Hugo continue to press the competitive case.

themes.title: Defense autonomy & drones
themes.description: New Trump administration tariffs on foreign drones sent AVAV and KTOS higher this week by shielding US makers from overseas rivals. Kratos added a US Army Javelin missile seeker-upgrade contract (Aug 6) and a potential $156M DOE Solar Shield counter-drone award on top of its raised FY26 guidance. Pentagon FY27 budget still requests ~$75B for unmanned/counter-drone systems.

themes.title: Field robotics
themes.description: Deere's autonomous articulated dump truck continues quarry operations under its 2nd-gen autonomy kit; Caterpillar's five-machine autonomous construction lineup remains in early rollout. Both remain diversified industrials where robotics is a small slice of the overall return.

themes.title: Japanese factory automation
themes.description: Fanuc shares have climbed back to ¥6,720 (from a 52-week low near ¥4,056) with analysts now 9-buy/1-sell and ~11% implied upside, as the market works through the Aug 3 guidance shock. Still too soon to call it a re-rating rather than a bounce.

themes.title: Supply chain & components
themes.description: Cognex declared a $0.085 dividend (ex-date Aug 20) even as shares chopped -3% on no fundamental news. MP Materials posted Q2 revenue of $108.5M (+89% YoY) but a GAAP net loss of $20.3M as magnet-ramp costs bite; shares still popped +8.6% on Aug 14 after management reiterated its mining-to-magnets roadmap at a Canaccord conference. Ouster's Q2 revenue accelerated 56% YoY to $55M, helped by a new Econolite/Utah DOT traffic-sensing contract.

themes.title: The robot "brain"
themes.description: NVIDIA's Jetson Thor platform remains generally available with 2M+ developers and adopters spanning Agility, Amazon Robotics, Boston Dynamics, Caterpillar, Figure, Hexagon, Medtronic and Meta. Skild AI shipped "Skild Brain 1.0," a 500B-parameter foundation model trained on data from 10,000 robots across 200+ hardware platforms, sharpening the race with Physical Intelligence (~$11B, in talks) to own the software layer.

themes.title: China scaling & listing
themes.description: Unitree's Shanghai STAR Market debut (ticker 688836) is confirmed for this week after a record 8,000x-oversubscribed retail tranche — China's first listed pure-play humanoid maker. BYD is entering the race with an August humanoid unveiling of its own. LimX ($2.2B pre-IPO) and Agibot continue prepping Hong Kong listings amid 150+ competing Chinese humanoid startups.

bear_case.title: Bubble warnings from serious sources
bear_case.description: China's NDRC has warned of a humanoid "bubble"; Morgan Stanley flags a wide gap between hype and scalability. UBS now forecasts only ~30,000 humanoids will ship globally in all of 2026 — a fraction of the volume the funding frenzy implies. The median disclosed humanoid round (Aug 2025-Jun 2026) was $145M, with rounds above $50M now 84% of all disclosed capital.

bear_case.title: Private marks don't always hold
bear_case.description: Hyundai just paid SoftBank $325M for its last Boston Dynamics stake, implying a $3.3B valuation for one of the industry's most established names — a fraction of Figure's headline $39B mark. Figure's own Forge secondary prices as of Aug 13 imply a softer number than the last primary round too. Private valuations can lag or overshoot reality for a long time before a real transaction corrects them.

bear_case.title: Demos ≠ autonomy
bear_case.description: If a humanoid demo isn't explicitly labeled autonomous, assume teleoperation. Dexterity, inference speed, reliability, and cost still confine real use to structured factory/warehouse tasks.

bear_case.title: Crowding & shakeout risk
bear_case.description: 150+ companies chasing humanoids; a reshuffling of startups is widely expected. Robotics pioneer Rodney Brooks argues much of the investment will be wasted.

bear_case.title: Guidance can evaporate fast
bear_case.description: Fanuc suffered its worst single-day fall in 40 years on Aug 3 despite Q1 profit +35%, purely on FY guidance missing estimates — shares have since partly recovered on renewed analyst buy ratings. ISRG is down 32.6% YTD despite beating Q2 estimates. MP Materials rallied 8.6% on management commentary alone, not on the GAAP net loss it just posted. In parts of this sector, sentiment is doing more work than fundamentals — in both directions.

bear_case.title: Revenue is elsewhere
bear_case.description: Industrial, logistics, and surgical robots generate proven revenue today; humanoids largely don't yet. Component and warehouse names carry less thesis risk than humanoid pure-plays.

bear_case.title: China price war
bear_case.description: Unitree's $5,900 R1 signals aggressive price compression that could squeeze Western OEM margins before the market matures — and 150+ Chinese humanoid startups, now including BYD, are competing on price and scale.

bear_case.title: "Dot-com stage" warnings
bear_case.description: KB Securities likened 2026's robotics/space enthusiasm to the final stage of the dot-com bubble; Ray Dalio separately compared the broader AI bubble to 1929 and 2000 valuation extremes. Sector EV/EBITDA multiples ranged from 0.9x (mature industrials) to 78.2x (speculative pure-plays) in Q4 2025 — a valuation split investors should not treat as one trade.
